---
applyTo: "src/ui/webview-react/components/workspace-viewer/**"
---

<purpose>
Workspace viewer is a full-screen modal for browsing/editing files and SCM state from the hosted dashboard. It mixes Zustand modal state with direct hosted-server HTTP calls, so path normalization and optimistic draft handling matter more than component structure.
</purpose>

<architecture>
- `WorkspaceViewerModal.tsx` is a portal with enter/exit animation state; closing the modal should clear transient loading/error flags through the store instead of relying on component unmount timing.
- Explorer and SCM panes call `utils/hostedApi.ts` directly. In hosted mode those requests carry the dashboard token; keep new endpoints in that helper instead of open-coding `fetch`.
- `workspaceViewerStore` caches unsaved file drafts by normalized workspace-relative path. Components should keep using those canonical keys, even if navigation starts from absolute paths or mixed separators.
</architecture>

<gotchas>
- `WorkspaceExplorerPane.tsx` deliberately normalizes Windows paths with case-insensitive workspace-root stripping so links emitted by AI output, Node, and the browser all resolve to the same selected file.
- File selection is request-sequenced and mobile editor visibility is store-driven. Avoid local component shortcuts that bypass `selectFile`, `setLoadedFileContent`, or pending-navigation handling.
- SCM actions refresh status first, then re-open the selected diff only if it still exists. Preserve that refresh-after-mutation flow so staged/unstaged lists and diff panes do not drift apart.
- Confirmation settings such as delete warnings come from `settingsStore.globalSettings`; do not add viewer-local copies.
- **`WorkspaceFileEditor.tsx` has no click handler of its own.** Its links and chips go through `CodeMirrorEditor`'s `createReferenceLinkHandlerExtension` and `openContextReferenceLink` with `{ inWorkspaceViewer: true }`, so every reference kind (commits, `$prior` previews, `/skill:`, `/mcp:`, secrets) and the plain-click-on-chip rule match the prompt editor. A local copy once drifted to Ctrl+Click-only and five kinds, which left chips dead. Previews opened from here render through `ContentPreviewModal`, which uses the elevated modal layer while the viewer is open.
- **Reference-link clicks in the hosted browser do not go through `MESSAGE_TYPES.OPEN_FILE`.** `openContextReference()` (`utils/contextReferenceActions.ts`) branches on `isStandalone`: in the VS Code panel it posts `OPEN_FILE` to the extension host; in the hosted browser (and inside `WorkspaceFileEditor.tsx`, via `inWorkspaceViewer`) it calls `workspaceViewerStore.openToFile()`/`openToDirectory()` instead, which resolves purely through `HostedWorkspaceViewerService`'s HTTP endpoints. A path-resolution fix on the VS Code side (`WebviewMessageRouter`/`PromptLinkProvider`) does **not** cover this path — multi-root folder-name-prefixed refs (`root2/src/index.ts`) must be handled by `HostedWorkspaceViewerService` itself.
- **Multi-root top level**: when the server reports `WorkspaceTreeResponse.isRootsList: true` (root path `""` in a multi-root workspace), every entry in the listing represents an entire workspace root, not a real file/subdirectory. `useWorkspaceExplorerContextMenu` disables Cut/Copy/Delete/Paste in that view (via its `isRootsList` option) — "Add to ctrlyoke" stays enabled since referencing a whole root as `@root2/` is meaningful. No other client-side path arithmetic changes were needed for multi-root browsing — the existing directory-listing/breadcrumb code already handles folder-name-prefixed paths correctly once the server returns them.
- **Multi-repo SCM**: `workspaceViewerStore` holds `repos`, `prefixRepoIds`, and `selectedRepoId` (all from `GET /api/workspace-viewer/repos`). `WorkspaceSourceControlPane` loads repos once on mount and re-runs `loadStatus`/`loadHistory` whenever `selectedRepoId` changes (both callbacks close over it and pass it to `workspaceStatus`/`workspaceCommitLog`). The repo picker lives at the top of `WorkspaceCommitArea` and renders **only when `repos.length > 1`**; `WorkspaceCommitArea` also threads `selectedRepoId` into commit/push/pull/generate, and history/checkout/git-ref-diff flows pass it too. `setRepos` defaults the selection (keep-if-still-valid → repo owning the open path → first repo). The "repo owning the open path" step reads the open path's first folder-name segment against the **server-supplied `prefixRepoIds` map** (`repoIdForPath`), never `repo.label`/`repo.id` — those diverge from the viewer-path prefix when a root sits below its git toplevel or several roots share one repo, so the client must not reverse-engineer the mapping. The **explorer** deliberately still calls `workspaceStatus()` with no repo (aggregate across all repos) for its gitDecoration coloring — do not scope that call. Panes unmount on tab switch, so the SCM pane's repo-scoped `sourceControlFiles` never clobbers the explorer's aggregate (each pane reloads on its own mount).
- **A new viewer tab is not done when the store union is widened.** `activeTab` is mirrored into the browser URL by `navigation/route.ts`, which owns `VIEWER_URL_TOKENS` — the single source for each tab's `viewer=` token (`explorer`/`scm`/`search`) and its inverse used by `parseRoute`. A tab missing an entry there serializes as some *other* tab's token, so the hosted dashboard silently switches tabs on reload or back/forward while everything looks correct in-session. Adding a tab means four coordinated edits: the token map, `normalizeRoute`/`deriveRoute` (which location fields, if any, the tab carries — Search carries none, its query is transient session state and not a shareable address), `applyRoute.ts`'s `applyViewer` (whose final branch is the SCM fallthrough, so an unhandled tab lands on Source Control), and `navTitle.ts`'s `locationLabel`.
- **Find All References is addressed by its origin, not its results.** The route carries `refs=<path>:<line>:<col>` (explorer tab only), and while it is set the normally inbound-only `lines` becomes the selected reference: `deriveRoute` emits it and `sameNavigation` compares it, which is what makes back/forward step through visited references. Restoring a route re-runs the query via `utils/languageReferences.ts` (cached per origin), which may have no editor on the origin file, so `withLanguageIntelligenceDocument` opens it on the server as a detached document; an editor that opens the same file later takes that document over. On mobile the panel's visibility is `languageReferencesPanelOpen`, which is deliberately not in the URL — a route with no selected reference opens it, one with a selection leaves it closed behind the explorer toolbar's references button.
- **ctrlyoke workflow files get their own completion layer in `WorkspaceFileEditor.tsx`** (`getCtrlYokeFileKind(filePath)`; every other file is untouched). `utils/workflowFileSupport/workflowFileCompletionExtension.ts` registers three sources (schema key/value, host-backed script/permission text, prompt tokens inside `PROMPT_TEXT`) as **language data**, never `autocompletion({ override })`, so they merge with `basicSetup`'s dropdown and a language server's; an `override` would drop the LSP source. They live in the `ctrlyokeFileSupport` compartment beside `languageIntelligenceCompartment`. CodeMirror tracks a completion source by function identity, so a source must be created once and not rebuilt inside `languageData.of(() => ...)` (an LSP stub that does loses its results every keystroke). The location/outline/completion modules, and with them the `yaml` parser, load through `loadWorkflowFileSupport()` (`import()`) the first time a ctrlyoke file opens; the sources answer nothing until the chunk arrives. Do not statically import `WorkflowDocumentLocation`, `WorkflowLocationYaml` or the completion core elsewhere in the webview or the first-paint bundle grows by the `yaml` package. The JSON half cannot use `jsonc-parser`'s `SyntaxKind` (an ambient `const enum`, rejected under the webview's `isolatedModules`), hence `JSON_TOKENS` in `WorkflowLocationJson.ts`. Script and permission requests reuse `SCRIPT_COMPLETIONS_REQUEST`/`PERMISSION_COMPLETIONS_REQUEST` with the field's own text slice and a position relative to it, numbered from 1,000,000,000 so the properties-panel editors (which match responses on `seq` alone) never consume them. Prompt-token inserts in a JSON workflow are escaped by the client's `escapeInsertText` option, which also covers the `#sym:` function-apply path.

</gotchas>
